description: Allonnia develops bioengineering solutions that harness microbial and enzymatic systems to remediate wastewater, soil, and mining residues while recovering valuable metals or neutralizing PFAS. Focusing on biologically driven remediation, their modular systems integrate seamlessly into existing industrial processes. Their dual emphasis on environmental restoration and resource recovery positions Allonnia as a new standard in efficient, nature-based circular economy technologies.

ARIX Technologies develops and operates specialized robotics to inspect pipelines and vessels for corrosion under insulation (CUI) without requiring excavation or shutdown. Their integrated hardware and data analytics platform streamlines detection, asset management, and repair planning while reducing costs and safety risks. ARIX serves petrochemical, refining, and energy clients with scalable CUI solutions and growing inspection deployments across North America.

DarkVision Technologies ( acquired by Koch Engineered Solutions (KES), a unit of Koch Industries Inc. ) develops the world’s most advanced acoustic imaging platforms for non-invasive inspection of energy and industrial infrastructure. Their systems capture ultra-high-resolution ultrasound data for pipes, wells, and tubulars—backed by AI and 3D visualization. DarkVision is positioned as a leader in asset integrity technology.

DISA Tech Corporation advances mineral processing through its patented High-Pressure Slurry Ablation platform. HPSA improves mineral liberation, recovery and product quality across mined ore, complex and lower-grade resources, and legacy materials. By capturing more value from every ton while reducing waste, DISA Tech helps expand the usable supply of minerals essential to industry and economic growth. DISA Uranium Corporation is redefining American uranium recovery and production. Headquartered in Casper, Wyoming, the Company recovers uranium and vanadium from abandoned uranium mine (AUM) waste, remediates legacy sites left across the western United States, and applies its exclusive, patented high-pressure slurry ablation technology (HPSA™) to make conventional uranium production cleaner, more efficient, and more economic. DISA Uranium holds the only U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) license to treat and recover AUM waste across multiple sites — and with a growing conventional resource base behind it, the Company is building the domestic capacity to turn American waste and American ore into American fuel. Our mission is simple: restore the past while powering the future, and rebuild a secure, independent domestic uranium supply chain.

e‑Zinc develops a zinc-based battery system engineered to store clean energy reliably for multiple days using abundant, recyclable materials. Their technology supports remote, off-grid, and grid-interconnected environments with scalable, low‑cost storage that reduces reliance on fossil fuels. e-Zinc's safety, availability, and minimal environmental footprint underpin their sustainability-first approach. With international recognition and leading investors backing their growth, e‑Zinc is actively advancing commercial deployments to accelerate the global transition to renewable energy.

Ebb has developed an electrochemical ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) approach that safely enhances seawater’s capacity to absorb atmospheric CO₂ by raising pH and promoting bicarbonate formation. This scalable and cost-competitive solution integrates with existing desalination and seawater processing facilities, enabling gigaton-scale carbon removal by leveraging the ocean’s vast surface area. In addition to removing CO₂ durably (for 10,000+ years), nutrient-neutral alkalinity reduces ocean acidification—benefiting marine ecosystems such as shellfish and coral.

Ekona Power has developed a scalable methane pyrolysis platform that splits natural gas into clean hydrogen and solid carbon with minimal emissions. Their process operates at low cost relative to electrolysis and integrates with existing gas infrastructure, accelerating transition to decarbonized hydrogen.

Expeto offers the "Nextworking" platform—combining private mobile networks, edge/cloud infrastructure, and IIoT applications—to give enterprises secure, real-time control of distributed assets. Their platform integrates seamlessly with existing public telecom networks and device ecosystems, enabling scalable, low-latency deployment for industries like utilities, manufacturing, and logistics. With a global market presence and growing customer base, Expeto is positioned as a leader in digital transformation connectivity.

HARBO Inc. is reshaping emergency response with ultra-fast containment solutions that stop spills before they become disasters. Our award-winning boom technology is trusted worldwide for its speed, simplicity, and reliability, empowering industries and communities to protect coastlines, assets, and ecosystems with confidence. What began as a bold idea has grown into a global movement for faster, smarter environmental protection.

Karbonetiq leverages industrial waste minerals to mineralize atmospheric carbon dioxide into stable carbonates, using passive airflow reactors that require no external energy. This modular CDR approach costs ~1/100th of conventional direct air capture methods and is scalable by co-locating on existing industrial sites.

Kelvin provides SaaS-based control software powered by AI/ML that allows engineers and operators to build, deploy, and run real-time control “SmartApps” across industrial assets. Their platform offers scalability (on any cloud or edge hardware), full operational visibility, and emissions tracking embedded in applications to reduce carbon footprint. Serving over 98 enterprise customers across 160,000+ jobs, Kelvin is accelerating the shift toward sustainable automation in heavy industries.

Koloma applies proprietary geological data analytics and exploration methods to unlock naturally occurring hydrogen trapped in subsurface rock formations. Their low-carbon, cost-effective hydrogen extraction platform provides a scalable source of clean energy that avoids electrolysis or fossil feedstocks. With leadership rooted in energy and geoscience expertise, Koloma is actively appraising assets to commercialize natural hydrogen resources for global decarbonization.

MineSense’s ShovelSense system integrates sensors, machine learning, and hardware to deliver real-time ore grade feedback during excavation, enabling miners to maximize metal recovery while minimizing waste and environmental impact. Their platform supports precise material sorting, blending, and processing control, resulting in increased operational efficiency and profitability. Headquartered in Vancouver and serving the global mining industry, MineSense is a trusted partner in modernizing mineral operations.

Moment Energy is the first and only company building commercial-scale battery energy storage from second-life EV batteries — fully certified across the UL safety stack and deployed in the field today. Moment's systems, which power data centers, hospitals, factories, and microgrids across North America, are sourced from batteries already on the continent's roads, manufactured in Texas and British Columbia. Moment partners with major automakers, including Mercedes-Benz Energy, to put retired EV batteries back to work before they're recycled.

Mosaic Materials specializes in using tunable metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to capture CO₂ from point sources or directly from the air. Developed from UC Berkeley research, their platform optimizes adsorption efficiency across energy scales and reduces the cost of carbon capture. Mosaic aims to support decarbonization in power generation, industrial processing, and direct air capture markets.

Osperity empowers industrial operations with AI-enabled visual monitoring that supports safety, security, and environmental compliance. Their platform manages smart camera networks, analyzes visuals using machine learning, and generates alerts across oil & gas, mining, and utility sectors. Customers benefit from reduced field visits, improved health, safety and environmental (HSE) tracking, and better operational efficiency.

Planetary introduces purified alkaline minerals into coastal outfall water to raise buffering capacity, enabling atmospheric CO₂ to permanently convert to bicarbonate and remain sequestered in the ocean. Their technology delivers the world’s first verified Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) carbon credits (sold to Shopify, Stripe, and British Airways), along with a published MRV protocol making them an industry pioneer. OAE integration with wastewater or desalination infrastructure enables scalable gigaton-scale carbon removal, while mitigating acidification and enhancing ocean health.

Quidnet’s Geomechanical Pumped Storage (GES) system pumps water into deep impermeable rock formations during periods of excess renewable energy and releases it later to generate electricity—offering multi-month duration storage with minimal water use. Successfully tested at the megawatt-hour scale with up to six months duration and funded by DOE and private investors, Quidnet promises commercial viability in long-duration energy resilience.

Rodatherm’s advanced geothermal system (AGS) transforms the Earth’s natural heat into on-demand, clean energy using closed-loop, engineered subsurface reservoirs. Unlike conventional geothermal, AGS does not require naturally occurring hydrothermal resources and can be deployed in a wide range of geologies. Rodatherm’s system delivers both high-temperature process heat and baseload electricity, offering a flexible and zero-emissions alternative to fossil fuels for heavy industry and the power grid. Their modular design supports scalable deployments across North America, while enabling 24/7 clean energy aligned with decarbonization goals.

Rotoliptic’s patented all-metal progressive cavity pumps deliver reliable, high-efficiency performance in extreme temperatures, high-viscosity and abrasive fluid applications. Their modular R65 and R200 series significantly reduce downtime and maintenance costs while lowering CO₂ emissions by up to 46% compared to conventional lift solutions. Based in British Columbia, Rotoliptic is pioneering next-gen fluid handling technologies for global oil & gas and industrial operations.

Sanctuary AI creates general-purpose robots designed with human-level dexterity, sensory capability, and AI-driven decision-making to perform economically meaningful work across industrial, logistics, and extraterrestrial environments. Founded by robotics and AI pioneers, Sanctuary’s robots aim to support safer, more productive workforces and enable new frontiers in productivity.

SensorUp offers methane emissions management solutions tailored to the oil and gas industry, combining geospatial data and environmental metrics to drive sustainability. Their emissions intelligence platform enables professionals to assess methane leakage, benchmark practices, and reduce environmental impact. The company is mission-driven to harness technology in the global effort toward decarbonization and compliance.

Summit Lithium (previously Summit Nanotech) has developed a leading direct lithium extraction (DLE) platform that extracts lithium from brine faster and with minimal water consumption, supporting both commercial-scale EV and battery supply chains. Their modular system and advanced sorbents deliver industry-leading purity and lower-levelized cost of lithium. Summit targets deployment across the Americas—including brine operations in Chile, Argentina, and the United States—while maintaining high ESG standards.

Syzygy Plasmonics is decarbonizing the chemical sector—responsible for 20% of industrial CO₂—by building light-powered reactors that replace thermal combustion. Its Rigel reactor channels light into high-efficiency photocatalysts to power reactions for e-fuels and hydrogen production. Designed for multiple chemistries, the platform supports ammonia cracking and CO₂-to-fuel applications.

Twelve is pioneering carbon transformation by converting captured CO₂ into critical products—such as jet fuel, plastics, and detergents—via electrochemical technology. Replacing fossil-derived inputs with air-based carbon, their solutions support sustainable manufacturing in aviation, automotive, and consumer goods. Twelve’s vision is a carbon-neutral supply chain for a world built from air.

VEERUM’s Visual Operations (VisOps) platform transforms industrial 3D and reality capture data into real-time, collaborative insights that improve performance and reduce site visits. It enables teams to visualize, manage, and analyze complex project environments from anywhere. Trusted by global operators in mining, energy, and infrastructure, VEERUM is redefining asset intelligence at scale.

Zero Industrial develops and operates thermal energy storage (TES) systems that electrify process heat applications in heavy industry without requiring customer capital investment. They deliver full project lifecycle execution—from engineering and permitting through operations—selling clean heat under Heat-as-a-Service contracts. Zero Industrial is advancing deployment across North America to reduce emissions from fossil-powered industrial facilities.

ZwitterCo’s advanced polymeric membranes use zwitterionic channels to resist fouling and restore filtration capability in challenging industrial effluents heavy in organics like BOD/COD and FOG. Their technology supports high-performance reuse and recovery applications across food, energy, and manufacturing sectors while lowering operational costs and chemical reliance. Built by a multidisciplinary team of over 60 membrane engineers and water treatment experts, ZwitterCo is driving scalable water innovation in high-strength process streams.
